summary: Auto-wah with eight filters (low-passes, peaks and two vocal formant filters) and 17 LFO shapes, the LFO free in Hz or locked to the tempo. Mono. The richest of the three wah machines.
use_for: Auto-wah with eight filters, including vowel-like ones, and many LFO shapes.
quirks: Mono, one track: NeoBuzz Live feeds it left + right summed. +3.3 dB at its defaults; default filter is Vocal I.
For the two vocal filters Cutoff is a vowel position, not a frequency: it is 0 to 240 across their formant tables.
LFO rate 240 to 254 lock to the tempo, 1 to 128 ticks a cycle; the sweeps then follow the song.
The Theviderness factor attribute (0 by default) scales resonance down at low cutoffs on the six non-vocal filters.

track_parameters.name: Cutoff
track_parameters.description: Cutoff before the LFO: 264 Hz x 32^(v/240), 264 Hz to 8.4 kHz, for the six low-pass and peak filters; for the vocal ones it is a vowel position (0 to 240).
track_parameters.how: Sets the filter's cutoff before the LFO: 264 Hz x 32^(v/240), 264 Hz to 8.4 kHz in 240 steps; for the two vocal filters it picks the vowel position instead.
track_parameters.sound: Low values give a dark, muffled sound; high values open it up. With a vocal filter it moves between vowel-like shapes.

track_parameters.name: Resonance
track_parameters.how: Sets the filter's resonance on a 0 to 240 scale (a Q from about 1 to 6); A machine attribute, Theviderness factor (0 by default), can scale resonance down at low cutoffs; at 0 it does nothing.
track_parameters.sound: More resonance gives a sharper, more vocal peak at the cutoff; too much rings and gets loud.

track_parameters.name: Filter
track_parameters.how: Chooses one of eight filters: two- and four-pole low-passes, three peak types and two vocal formant filters.
track_parameters.sound: The low-passes cut the top and wah around the cutoff, the peaks boost around it, and the two vocal ones give vowel-like movement.

track_parameters.name: LFO rate
track_parameters.description: LFO rate [Hz]. 0.05–26.3 Hz exponential up to 239; 240–254 lock the LFO to the tempo instead: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 28, 32, 48, 64, 96 or 128 ticks a cycle, as its own text says
track_parameters.how: Sets the LFO speed: 0.05 Hz to 26 Hz exponential up to 239, then 240 to 254 lock it to the tempo at 1 to 128 ticks a cycle.
track_parameters.sound: Slow rates give a long filter breathing; the locked values keep the sweep in time with the song.

track_parameters.name: LFO mod
track_parameters.how: Sets how far the LFO moves the cutoff: it swings plus or minus half this many steps, each step 1/48 of an octave, so 240 is plus or minus 2.5 octaves.
track_parameters.sound: Low values give a gentle wobble; high values give a wide, obvious wah sweep. At 0 the cutoff stays where Cutoff puts it.

track_parameters.name: LFO Shape
track_parameters.how: Chooses the LFO wave from 17: sine, saws, square, triangle, four odd blends, stepped waves and two random ones.
track_parameters.sound: A sine sweeps smoothly, a saw sweeps then snaps back, a square jumps between two cutoffs, and the random shapes give an unpredictable wobble.

track_parameters.name: Inertia
track_parameters.how: Sets how slowly the cutoff chases its target, 0 to 60: higher values glide more slowly (a step of 10 x e^(-9 v / 240) cutoff steps per 64 samples).
track_parameters.sound: Low values follow the LFO exactly; high values round off the sweep and smooth out jumps from a pattern change.

track_parameters.name: Set phase
track_parameters.description: Writing it sets the LFO's position in its cycle: 2 pi x v / 128, up to 357 degrees (255 = not written).
track_parameters.how: Writing a value sets the LFO's position in its cycle: 2 pi x v / 128, 0 to 357 degrees (255 means not written).
track_parameters.sound: Use it to start the sweep from the same place on every bar.
